parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Implementation swarm ended completed 1 and aborted 3; required modules were absent and official evaluation scored 0 of 70.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent and probe children recognized the need to emulate PyYAML safe_load/dump, ESM modules, manual --a parsing, and no external dependencies.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor also recognized the same PyYAML and Node ESM requirements and spent most of the run probing exact behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement understanding was broadly similar; the difference was execution, with parallel reaching partial implementation and serial never writing deliverables.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split work into four probe-only children, then four implementation owners for resolve, loader, dumper, and argparse/entry.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial remained a single-actor effort and planned a local multi-module architecture only after extensive probing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used explicit per-module ownership but deferred implementation until a second swarm; serial had no child ownership boundaries and no delegated lifecycle.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The implementation swarm was launched with a shared module contract and an entry child wrote imports for loader and dumper modules.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all context in one actor and had no cross-agent interface handoff or module-contract boundary.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel depended on cross-child module delivery, but the downstream modules were not completed; serial had no interface mismatch because no files were produced.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote resolve.mjs plus argparse.mjs and test13.mjs, while loader.mjs and dumper.mjs never materialized.

comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; the only actor was cancelled while still active.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost necessary child implementation work at the child lifecycle boundary, whereas serial lost the whole single actor before producing artifacts.

comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel verification was component-local and incomplete; serial verification was only reference probing with no produced solution.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome: both completed official evaluations failed 0/70. Parallel produced a partial artifact through completed child work but lost the loader and dumper implementations when the implementation swarm was cancelled. Serial spent the run on a single long probing and planning trajectory and was cancelled before writing any artifact files.
parallel_contributors: Probe-only first swarm deferred implementation into the later closure window.
Active implementation children for loader, dumper, and resolve verification were cancelled, leaving a partial module set.
serial_contributors: The single serial actor spent the whole run probing and planning and did not write the deliverable before timeout.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel delivered an entry point and two library files; serial delivered no files.
Neither run completed a full YAML loader/dumper implementation capable of satisfying the benchmark.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative explanation for two failed attempts, not an outcome-differential root cause

candidates.reason: Implementation was assigned to implementation children for resolve, loader, dumper, and CLI/entry modules; the failure was incomplete/cancelled execution, not no implementer.
The parent launched a module-contract implementation swarm and the entry child imported the intended module interfaces; no completed incompatible components needed an unassigned integrator.
The entry file owner existed and wrote test13.mjs; missing loader and dumper modules came from aborted children, not an unowned final entry point.
The parent orchestrator owned the probe-to-implementation pipeline; the adverse event was deferred implementation and cancellation before the pipeline could close, not absent ownership.
The observed gate was not one mandatory serial preflight or oracle; four investigation agents ran as a separate phase before implementation.

The parallel parent used the first swarm only for behavioral investigation, waited for all four reports, and only afterward launched the implementation swarm. That deferred productive module work into the closing window; this is adverse in the parallel run but does not explain a pass/fail difference because the serial run also failed.
candidates.realized_consequence: Implementation began only after the completed probe-only phase, leaving no remaining parent-led integration or end-to-end verification window before timeout.
candidates.near_match_reason: The gate was not one mandatory serial preflight or oracle; it was a completed multi-agent investigation phase whose findings preceded all implementation work.
